title: Rearchitect async queue topology for stability and predictable retries
creator: Alicia Park
description:
Summary:
We have ongoing reliability and performance issues tied to our mixed Redis/Kafka async topology: sporadic duplicate work during Redis visibility timeout races, cascading backlog spikes when downstream services degrade, and retry behavior that exacerbates bursts. This ticket refactors the async processing topology to reduce duplicated work, make retries predictable with exponential backoff + jitter, add explicit backpressure controls, and upgrade Redis/Kafka clients to the latest vetted versions.

Goals:
- Eliminate class of duplicate processing resulting from visibility timeout races and worker restarts.
- Implement deterministic retry semantics across both Redis-based delayed queues and Kafka consumers (exponential backoff + jitter, configurable max attempts).
- Introduce backpressure signals that let the router/nginx and worker pool slow intake (circuit-breaker style) rather than pile up unbounded queues.
- Replace bespoke delayed-queue logic with a single topology pattern: primary Kafka topic for incoming work, dead-letter + retry topics, and a lightweight Redis index for short-lived dedupe tokens when necessary.
- Upgrade Redis client from ioredis 4.x to 5.x and Kafka client from node-rdkafka 3.x to librdkafka-backed client 4.x (or equivalent in Go runtime), addressing known memory leak and reconnect bugs.
- Add SLO-focused telemetry: work age histogram, retry count distribution, visibility-timeout collision rate, consumer lag and processing latency per partition.

Approach & implementation plan:
1) Design doc: "Async topology: Kafka-first, Redis for dedupe" (Confluence link: https://confluence.redwood/async-topology-2026).
2) Create new Kafka retry topics pattern: <topic>-retry-1, <topic>-retry-2 with increasing delay computed by consumer header and a small scheduler service for re-enqueueing. Configurable retry policy with backoff factors and jitter.
3) Consumer changes: switch consumers to cooperative rebalancing, track in-flight message IDs and short-lived Redis dedupe keys (TTL = 2x max processing time) to avoid duplicate processing across restarts.
4) Visibility timeout & ack semantics: move ack decision point to after persistence of side-effects and checkpoint to ensure once-only semantics where possible; in idempotent paths accept at-least-once with dedupe keys.
5) Backpressure controls: expose backlog thresholds in the router and a worker controller that dynamically scales worker pool and can return 429/503 with Retry-After when saturation is detected. Integrate with Autoscaler to inform Dedicated capacity burst.
6) Client upgrades: perform staged upgrades in a canary cluster, monitor memory and reconnect metrics, and roll out across regions.
7) Observability: new dashboards and alerts (Grafana/Tempo) for consumer_lag > X, retry_rate spike, duplicate_processing_rate > 0.1%, and tail latency regressions.
8) Testing: unit tests, integration tests with local Kafka (testcontainers), long-running soak test (48h) in staging with synthetic traffic patterns that reproduce prior incidents.

Migration & rollout strategy:
- Phase A (canary): Deploy new consumer library + retry topic logic to 5% of partitions in staging. Run soak tests and validate metrics.
- Phase B (regional canary): Enable in one low-traffic region; run production shadow traffic for 24h.
- Phase C (gradual rollout): Increase to 50% partitions, then full. Employ feature flag to toggle dedupe index and backpressure behaviors separately.
- Rollback plan: revert to previous consumer binary and pause retry-scheduler; promote old clients if duplicates regress.

Acceptance criteria:
- Duplicate processing measured by dedupe-key collisions reduced to <0.05% over 24h test window under 2x normal QPS.
- End-to-end retry count distribution matches configured backoff policy with median retry delay within +/-20% of target.
- Consumer lag and processing latency stable or improved compared to baseline in runtime-1.20.
- No memory/regression errors from client library upgrades during 48h canary.
- Monitoring dashboards and runbook updated; on-call run through playbook and can successfully throttle a synthetic overload.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Introducing retry-topics increases complexity and storage costs. Mitigation: TTL-based compaction and automated cleanup jobs; start with conservative retention.
- Risk: Redis dedupe adds another point of failure. Mitigation: Redis used only for short-lived tokens and gracefully degraded to at-least-once processing if unavailable; flag to disable dedupe.
- Risk: Upgrade triggers unknown client-side bug. Mitigation: staged canary + memory profiling + telemetry gating.

Estimate breakdown (8 points):
- Design & reviews: 1.5
- Core consumer+retry implementation: 3
- Client library upgrades & canary: 1.5
- Observability & tests: 1
- Rollout + runbook updates: 1
